claim: Subtle CRD features, including hydrophobic and charged clusters, govern recognition of complex tumor-associated antigens such as the Tn antigen in Vatairea macrocarpa lectin (VML).
falsifier: The claim can be tested by mutating hydrophobic/charged residues in the CRD of VML and measuring binding affinity to Tn antigen.

conditions: High-resolution structures of native and recombinant VML with Tn antigen and GalNAc
exclusions: Evidence is limited to VML lectin studied in the reported experiments; transfer to other lectins is unestablished.

title: Subtle CRD features for recognition of complex tumor-associated

claim: In the quantum verification protocol, the number of bits the verifier still misses at the end of the protocol increases with proof size N, indicating that the verification problem becomes more difficult for classical computation as N increases.
falsifier: Vary N in the protocol and measure the verifier's residual missed bits after the protocol to confirm the increasing trend and its relation to classical difficulty.

conditions: protocol is the reported prover-verifier interactive setting
verifier receives limited information about the proof
proof is provided as unentangled quantum states
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported protocol, parameter ranges, and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Increasing proof size N–number of bits missed principle
